multi_tenant_model.tenant_customer: customer owned and managed by the tenant
multi_tenant_model.rule: A tenant customer is never a ROTAS platform tenant and never authorizes cross-tenant access.

methodology.threat_model: OWASP four-question framework with STRIDE categories

privacy.legal_posture: Controller, processor, lawful-basis, retention and data-subject obligations require documented legal validation for Mozambique and each tenant contract.

minimum_controls: encryption in transit and at rest

data_flows.flow: Manager browser -> same-origin BFF -> tenant API -> PostgreSQL RLS
Driver device -> scoped offline store -> sync API -> PostgreSQL RLS

data_flows.purpose: audited governance workflows with minimized payloads

data_flows.flow: tenant API and workers -> email or messaging provider
services -> logs, metrics and error monitoring
data_flows.purpose: security and reliability operations without business payload or PII

data_flows.flow: PostgreSQL and object storage -> encrypted backup -> isolated restore
data_flows.purpose: disaster recovery under the original tenant authorization boundary

data_flows.flow: transactional stores -> tenant-scoped BI read models
data_flows.purpose: tenant analytics; read models never write operational state

required_open_work: Approve a legal role and responsibility matrix for ROTAS and each tenant.
Version purpose, lawful basis, retention and deletion policy per data category.
Implement tenant-scoped access, correction, export, restriction and deletion workflows where legally applicable.
Define immutable-record exceptions for fiscal, audit, payroll and safety evidence.
Prove cryptographic deletion or key revocation for tenant offboarding, including replicas, caches, objects and backups.
Contract and assess subprocessors for storage, telemetry, email and messaging.
Prohibit production personal data in local development, test fixtures and performance reports.

release_policy.pentest_target: deployed release-candidate SHA in production-like staging

threats.title: Cross-tenant object access and tenant confusion
threats.scenario: An authenticated tenant supplies another tenant identifier or an overlapping object identifier and reads or mutates that tenant's customer data.
existing_controls: TenantPrincipal is derived from the authenticated token rather than a client-selected tenant header.
Service-layer tenant checks and strict not-found responses limit enumeration.
PostgreSQL FORCE RLS provides a second boundary.
required_verification: Two-tenant authenticated API pentest with overlapping identifiers
Restricted rotas_app RLS proof for every tenant table and relation

threats.title: Application connection bypasses PostgreSQL RLS
threats.scenario: The API starts with a superuser or BYPASSRLS database role, making application defects cross-tenant.
existing_controls: Production startup rejects superuser or BYPASSRLS DATABASE_URL.
rotas_app is NOBYPASSRLS; rotas_admin is separated for controlled jobs and migrations.
required_verification: Inspect current_user and rolbypassrls in the deployed RC
Exercise RLS below the API

threats.title: Platform control-plane confused deputy
threats.scenario: A platform token is accepted by a tenant route, or support uses broad cross-tenant access without a purpose-bound grant.
existing_controls: Platform and tenant JWT scopes are separated.
Platform support reads are audited and privileged writes are role-restricted.
required_verification: Implement approved JIT break-glass grant with tenant, reason, expiry and revocation
Pentest every platform role against tenant endpoints

threats.title: Browser token theft, CSRF or BFF bypass
threats.scenario: Script injection, forged same-site requests or a direct public API call steals/replays a session or bypasses the Manager authorization boundary.
existing_controls: Manager uses same-origin BFF and HttpOnly cookies.
Static boundary gate blocks browser token storage, Authorization headers and direct API URLs.
required_verification: DAST for XSS, CSRF, cookie attributes, origin validation and cache behavior
Verify security headers on staging edge

threats.title: Lost driver device leaks offline tenant data
threats.scenario: A lost, shared or re-paired device retains another driver or tenant's jobs, tokens, photos, cache or queued operations.
existing_controls: Dexie, sync and cache identity include tenant, driver and session.
Logout clears tokens, tables, caches and Workbox queue fail-closed.
required_verification: Real-device lost/offline/re-pair journey
Define device encryption, remote revocation and retention requirements

threats.title: Replay or sync conflict creates duplicate business effects
threats.scenario: Retried HTTP or offline operations duplicate payments, stock consumption, delivery or workshop transitions.
existing_controls: HTTP and offline operations carry idempotency identity.
Mutation, audit, outbox and response share a transaction for covered critical commands.
required_verification: Inventory every critical mutating endpoint
Concurrency and retry tests against the deployed RC with Redis/network faults

threats.title: Object storage key confusion or malicious upload
threats.scenario: A user obtains another tenant's object, uploads active content or malware, or reuses an over-broad presigned URL.
existing_controls: File metadata is tenant-scoped and upload MIME/size are restricted.
Production startup requires configured object storage.
required_verification: Test object-key and presign isolation with two tenants
Add content scanning/quarantine and safe download headers
Prove bucket policy and encryption

threats.title: Unsafe upstream request, proxy abuse or SSRF
threats.scenario: A crafted URL or upstream response makes the BFF/backend contact internal services, leak credentials or follow an untrusted redirect.
existing_controls: Manager upstream helper uses configured destinations and typed timeout/error behavior.
Production configuration validates external URLs.
required_verification: SSRF, DNS rebinding, redirect and request-smuggling pentest
Document outbound allowlists and metadata-service denial

threats.title: Outbox or Governance event spoofing and replay
threats.scenario: A forged, altered or replayed event creates duplicate cases or an unauthorized governance transition.
existing_controls: Transactional outbox, schema validation, API key authentication and idempotent conflict semantics are implemented.
DLQ/replay is audited and concurrency-controlled.
required_verification: Rotate and scope integration credentials
Staging replay, tamper and schema-confusion tests against real Governance

threats.title: Financial, stock or workshop state tampering
threats.scenario: A user bypasses lifecycle gates, changes immutable financial evidence or creates negative/incorrect stock.
existing_controls: Domain state transitions, database constraints and immutable ledger triggers protect covered flows.
Workshop billing and delivery are fail-closed around QC and financial conditions.
required_verification: Privilege matrix and workflow abuse pentest
Reconcile stock, journals and invoices after concurrency/fault injection

threats.title: Sensitive data leaks through telemetry or diagnostics
threats.scenario: PII, payroll, tokens, request bodies or tenant identifiers are exported to logs, Sentry, metrics or performance evidence.
existing_controls: Sentry before_send scrubs named PII fields.
Performance reports redact authorization and diagnostics reject production.
Observability validator forbids sensitive/high-cardinality labels.
required_verification: Canary-secret and synthetic-PII leakage test across logs/traces/errors/metrics
Field-level data classification review

threats.title: Dependency, build or image supply-chain compromise
threats.scenario: A vulnerable or replaced dependency/image executes in the Manager, Driver, API or Governance runtime.
existing_controls: Staging base images are digest-pinned and the build runbook requires SBOM, provenance, signature and admission verification.
Dependency audit is recorded without false mitigation.
required_verification: Close PR-18 high/critical advisories
Verify signed RC digests, SBOM and provenance in remote CI/registry

threats.title: Resource exhaustion and tenant noisy-neighbor
threats.scenario: A tenant or unauthenticated actor exhausts workers, database pool, exports, uploads, sync or third-party quotas.
existing_controls: Selected endpoints use rate limiting, bounded jobs and timeouts.
Performance budgets and SLO alerts are versioned.
required_verification: Authenticated per-tenant quota and abuse tests
Two-hour RC soak and worker/pool saturation tests
Verify edge rate limits

threats.title: Backup or restore crosses confidentiality boundary
threats.scenario: Backup media, restore credentials or a copied production dataset leaks; restore loses tenant isolation or immutable records.
existing_controls: Local DR tooling encrypts backup and validates schema, FORCE RLS and accounting balance after isolated restore.
required_verification: Object-locked cross-region storage and independent operator drill
PITR, key rotation and authorized production-volume restore

threats.title: Privacy lifecycle, export and tenant offboarding failure
threats.scenario: Data is retained, exported, deleted or transferred without a defined purpose, authority, immutable-record exception or complete propagation to caches, objects and backups.
existing_controls: Tenant scoping exists for operational records.
Audit retention cleanup is configurable and bounded.
required_verification: Approved privacy/legal matrix
Tenant-scoped data inventory and DSAR/export/offboarding E2E
Retention and deletion evidence across all stores

threats.title: BI, AI or third-party integration breaks tenant or purpose boundary
threats.scenario: Analytics, recommendations, email or messaging mixes tenants, exports excessive fields, or writes operational state outside audited domain commands.
existing_controls: BI is designed as tenant-scoped read-derived data.
Accepted recommendations must return through audited domain APIs.
Notifications are queued through controlled workers.
required_verification: Cross-tenant BI and export tests
Subprocessor contracts and data minimization review
Prove analytics cannot write operational tables

pentest.independence: Tester must be independent from the implementation team.
prerequisites: Written authorization and rules of engagement
acceptance: No open critical or high finding
Final report binds target, timestamp, RC SHA and tester
Residual medium/low risks have owner and target date
